title: MWSS-171 constructed a vertical take-off and landing pad
description: Marine Wing Support Squadron 171 improved their combat readiness in the cold mountains of Higashihiroshima, Japan during Exercise Kamoshika Wrath 17-1. Lance Corporal Emma Norris headed to the field to bring you the story. This story includes soundbites from Staff Sgt. Richard Bassitt, Bluffton, Ohio, and Capt. Kevin Wheeler, Gloucester, Massachusetts. This story is also available in high definition.

transcript.text: - [Emma] Service members with Marine Wing Support
Squadron 171 constructed a vertical takeoff and landing pad
during exercise Komashika Wrath 17 Tac One.
- Ideally what it could be used for at a five,
we lay the matting down and then you could bring
in helos for cas evacs, or you could set up a point
for either Cobras or Hueys to come in and land
and refuel, and then take back off and take
the fight to the enemy.
- [Emma] Installing the Vitol pad helped
train the marines in different areas
of aviation ground support.
- It wasn't an easy install.
There was a lot of mud, there was a lot of dirt,
marines had to get in there and pick the mud
out of the little crevices between the AM2 pads
before the pads actually fell into place.
7011s had to make sure that everybody
was lined up correctly, making sure
that the locking bars are,
I mean, it was a complicated process,
and the marines executed with discipline.
You could tell that they were challenged,
but every night they were out there until 2200,
and they were back up the next morning
at zero six to continue the work,
and they did it with discipline,
and I'm really proud of 'em.
- [Emma] MWSS 171 trains often to sustain
their combat readiness to help support the mission
of Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni.
Reporting from Haromar, Japan, I'm Lance Corporal
Emma Norris.
